_notice: Coach notes in the structure of the coach content form (Sections A to D), in the voice set out under 'voice'. Reviewed and approved by the MTB east crew on 16 October 2026 (docs/Sofa-to-Singletrack-Coach-Notes-FOR-REVIEW-2026-10-16.pdf). Change the words only with the crew's say-so.
welcome: Welcome aboard, {name}. Your first session, {sessionName}, is a gentle one on purpose. No pressure, just get a feel for the bike.

early._notice: Weeks 1 to 3. Deliberately unconditional: nothing about the plan changes, whatever the rider says.
early.Easier than expected: Good sign. It means the base fitness is there. Don't jump ahead of the plan yet though; the next few weeks build for a reason. Just enjoy feeling strong and stick with what's coming next.
early.About right: That's exactly where we want you in these first few weeks. Keep showing up at this effort and the fitness will build itself, nothing to change.
early.Tougher than expected: Normal this early on: your body's adapting to something new. Don't chase the plan's pace if it doesn't feel right; slow it down, and it'll click over the next couple of sessions.
early.Had to stop early: That happens. Plenty of people need a session or two to find their legs. Have a look at your bike setup (saddle height, tyre pressure) in case that's part of it, and go into the next one without expecting anything.
early.Didn't get to it: Completely fine. The first few weeks are about building the habit, not hitting a perfect record. Just pick back up with the next one.

later._notice: Week 4 onwards. The notes ask the rider to change their own effort; the app never changes the plan's minutes.
later.Easier than expected: Nice. That's a sign to push a little harder next time out. Try holding a slightly higher effort on your next session and see how that feels.
later.About right: That's the effort we want to see this deep into the plan. Keep it right there for your next session.
later.Tougher than expected: Worth backing off slightly on your next session: ease the pace or shorten it a touch, and don't be afraid to walk sections that aren't clicking.
later.Had to stop early: If that's happened more than once recently, it's worth taking your next session properly easy. Sometimes the body just needs a lighter week. One easier session won't undo your progress.
later.Didn't get to it: No guilt needed. Life gets in the way. Just get back on for the next one whenever you can.

situations.descents: Look through the corner or the section ahead, not down at your front wheel. Where your eyes go, the bike tends to follow. Start slower than feels necessary; speed comes with confidence, not the other way round.
situations.joints: A bit of new-activity discomfort in the first couple of weeks isn't unusual, but anything sharp, one-sided, or that doesn't ease off deserves a proper check from a physio or GP rather than pushing through it.
situations.climbs: Everyone's got a different engine. The point is to ride your own pace and get to the top however long it takes. Sit slightly further back and keep pedalling smoothly rather than mashing the gear.
situations.motivation: This happens to everyone at some point. Don't try to catch up on missed sessions. Just get back on for the next one on the plan and let the momentum build again naturally.
situations.equipment: Most early wobbles come down to saddle height (should let your leg almost straighten at the bottom of the pedal stroke) or tyre pressure (softer than road bikes, but not so soft it feels vague). Worth a quick check before assuming it's you.
situations.weather: Riding in the wet or wind is a genuinely useful skill to build, but if it's unsafe (ice, high winds, thunder), swap to the indoor/trainer option for that session rather than risk it.
situations.comparison: Everyone on this plan started from a different point. The only comparison that matters is you against where you were a few weeks ago.

raceWeek.taper: Feeling like you haven't done enough this week is completely normal. The whole point of a taper is doing less, so your legs are fresh. Trust the rest.
raceWeek.dayBefore: Get your kit and bike sorted the night before so the morning is calm. Eat a meal you know agrees with you, and try to get a decent night's sleep. Nerves are normal and won't stop you riding well.
raceWeek.raceMorning: Nerves before a first race are completely normal, even for people who've raced for years. Remember the goal today is finishing your own race, at your own pace. Enjoy it.

junior._notice: Sofa to Singletrack Juniors: every line here is written to the grown-up riding with the child, not to the child. Reviewed and approved by the MTB east crew on 16 October 2026 together with the adult notes.
junior.welcome: Welcome, {name}'s grown-up. The first game, {sessionName}, is short on purpose: fifteen minutes, somewhere flat, and you count out loud. Helmet on before the bike moves, and stay within sight the whole time. When it is done, tick it here and {name} collects the first badge.

checkins._notice: The grown-up answers for the child after each game. Nothing medical, nothing about pushing harder.
checkins.Loved it: That is the whole plan working. Nothing to change: same place, next game, and let them tell someone about the badge.
checkins.Fine: Fine is good. Fine means it was not scary and not boring. The next game adds one small thing, so keep the pace and the place the same.
checkins.Found it hard: Play the same game again before moving on, somewhere flatter if you can, and stop while they are still enjoying it. The badge is for trying, not for perfect. If it was the standing or the braking that was hard, lower the saddle a touch.
checkins.Had to stop early: Stopping early is fine and you made the right call. Next time out, halve the number of goes and finish with something they already like doing. A short, happy session beats a long one every time.
checkins.Didn't get to it this week: Nothing lost. The game is still there and so is the badge. Pick a day this week, keep it short, and do the same game rather than skipping ahead.

raceWeek.taper: Race week for a Junior is a normal week with shorter games. Nothing new to learn now: a lap of the park, a whistle stop or two, and plenty of talking about what race day looks like, so nothing is a surprise.
raceWeek.dayBefore: Bike checked together tonight, helmet and clothes laid out, a snack packed. Tell them the plan for the morning in order: park, sign on, look at the course, line up, ride, cake. Early night for everyone.
raceWeek.raceMorning: Fun race means fun race. Get there with time to walk a bit of the course together, remind them where you will be standing, and that finishing is the whole job. Take the photo at the finish, not the start.

junior.graduation: Sixteen games, sixteen badges, and a child who rides a trail standing up. A fun race is next if they want it, and the whole plan works again at the next age up: same games, bigger child, longer laps.

voice.always: Keep it plain, practical and specific: real advice you'd say trackside, not generic hype. End on something forward-looking (the next session) instead of a pat on the back.
voice.avoid: No exclamation-mark enthusiasm, no fitness-app clichés ("crush it", "you've got this"), no medical claims.
